speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger. To begin my evaluation, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a classic injury mechanism for a jersey finger. Did the finger get stuck when you pulled back, or did it just swell up immediately? Also, can you show me exactly where the pain is most severe? REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Avulsion Injury of the Flexor Digitorum Profundus). The clinical presentation of a forced extension injury followed by an inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint is pathognomonic. I am requesting an MRI of the right hand to confirm the tendon avulsion and assess the size of the tendon retraction.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
